examples.prompt:

Create a SINGLE transparent PNG sprite sheet, landscape 1536x1024, exactly THREE columns by TWO rows of 512x512 cells. Six consecutive stages of ONE COMPLETE ACTION, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. These six images play QUICKLY at 180ms per frame, followed by the first frame for closure. Show a real activity progressing over TIME, not six disconnected views of a stationary object.
Input image 1 is the identity and engraving-style reference. Redraw the same complete subject coherently in every frame in its original hand-colored copperplate engraving style. Preserve its identity, proportions, palette, fine hatching and mechanical construction. Allow tiny handmade contour differences, but not shape mutation. Full subject in each cell, comparable scale and shared anchor. Every drawing must fit within 420x420 pixels centered in its cell, at least 46 pixels transparent margin on all sides. Never cross cell boundaries.
TRUE TRANSPARENT background, no opaque paper, no ground shadow or scenery. Paper and captions are supplied separately by the product. No grid, borders, labels, added text, motion lines, blur, physical cards, or cinematic effects. Exactly SIX complete poses.
Subject: the complete antique gramophone in the reference: large golden brass horn opening toward upper LEFT, curved dark metal support/tonearm assembly on the RIGHT, black record on the wooden box, dark brown paneled wooden cabinet, front-right winding crank. Preserve the entire horn rim, stem, tonearm, soundbox, record, cabinet and crank in every frame. Keep exactly the SAME front three-quarter camera and cabinet alignment in all six cells. The cabinet and horn stay fixed; this is mechanical operation, never a camera orbit.
Timeline: 1 ready to play: crank handle low, soundbox just raised above outer record rim. 2 winding starts: crank turns one third of a revolution around its front-right pivot, record turns and soundbox lowers to the outer groove. 3 crank advances another third turn, record advances, tonearm begins its small inward tracking arc. 4 crank completes the full winding turn, record advances, tonearm tracks a little farther inward. 5 winding stops with handle low, record still turns, soundbox begins to rise slightly at the end of this short illustrative playback burst. 6 soundbox returns to its ready position just above outer rim, crank handle low, close to pose 1.
Make the crank's three different radial positions visually clear at small size, with mechanically connected bent shaft and handle, not a detached or bending cabinet. Show crisp changing record-groove highlights as the record rotates, no added record label or symbols. A small coherent tonearm arc supports the main crank rotation; horn and cabinet must never flip, resize, tilt or wobble. No people, hands, faces, extra objects, music notes, extra horns, duplicate tonearms or missing parts.
